title: Banks' AI gains and AI risk are now the same story
dek: DNB cut 400 technology jobs to agentic AI this week, Evident's index showed bank AI scores accelerating, and Korea's regulators say AI-assisted attackers are now testing the same financial firms those agents touch.

body.head: Efficiency gains get a body count
body.text: DNB said it is reducing its Technology & Services workforce by about 400 jobs: Know Your Customer work and coding are the two areas where AI agents already contribute "substantial efficiency gains." That is a specific, attributable number tied to two named areas, which is rarer than most AI-productivity claims banks make.
support: In order to deliver better customer experiences, increase efficiency and meet customers’ future needs, DNB is carrying out organisational changes and downsizing as part of a comprehensive restructuring of Technology & Services (T&S).
At the same time, the Group has adopted agentic AI in several parts of its operations.

Control of customer data and the work relating to the Know Your Customer (KYC) process, as well as technology development and coding, are areas where the bank is already seeing that AI agents can contribute substantial efficiency gains.
The changes entail a reduction in the workforce of about 400 full-time equivalents (FTEs).

body.head: The index says the same
body.text: That lines up with what Evident's AI Index found this year: the average bank score across its ranking rose 26%, nearly three times the pace of previous years. BBVA, which the index ranks first among eurozone banks, says software development productivity is up close to 28% and that seventy-five percent of employees already use generative AI on a recurring basis.
support: BBVA is the bank with the most mature artificial intelligence strategy in Spain and the eurozone, according to the international Evident AI Index.
Under this methodology, BBVA ranks first among eurozone banks and third among all European banks.
Seventy-five percent of employees use generative AI on a recurring basis , saving an average of around 2.4 hours per week on repetitive, lower-value tasks.
it is accelerating software development through a model in which people and agents collaborate throughout the entire lifecycle, already delivering productivity improvements of close to 28%.
The average bank score rose 26%, nearly three times the pace of previous years.

body.head: More data goes to work
body.text: Plaid's answer this week is to put more of that data to work: LendScore 2 uses cash flow underwriting to predict a borrower's ability to repay a loan with 42% greater strength than traditional credit data alone, and a new foundation model purpose-built for fraud is trained on patterns from the Plaid Network.
support: Another new model, LendScore 2 (Ls2), uses cash flow underwriting and predicts a borrower’s ability to repay a loan with 42% greater strength than with traditional credit data alone, the release said.
Plaid also announced Tuesday the availability of a new AI foundation model that is purpose-built for fraud and trained on patterns and data points from the Plaid Network.

body.head: The same firms are targets
body.text: Korea's financial authorities issued a consumer alert and began a monthlong response effort this week after suspected AI-assisted cyberattacks stole personal information from seven financial firms, including Shinhan Bank and Hyundai Capital. Regulators now suspect the attackers are scanning a broad range of companies for weaknesses rather than pursuing a single target, so brokerages, insurers and card issuers are checking their own exposure.
support: Financial authorities issued a consumer alert at the “caution” level Tuesday and began a monthlong response effort after suspected AI-assisted cyberattacks stole personal information from seven financial firms.
The seven affected firms are Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Hana Bank, BNK Busan Bank, Yegaram Savings Bank, Welcome Savings Bank and Hyundai Capital.

The digital risk analysis team at the FSS has identified about 30 IP addresses associated with the attacks across multiple countries and territories including the United States, Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Spain, Latvia, Sweden, Germany and Korea.

Attempted intrusions detected across several parts of the financial sector have led regulators and industry officials to suspect that the attackers were scanning a broad range of companies for weaknesses rather than pursuing a single target.
Amid growing concerns, brokerages, insurers and credit card issuers are stepping up security measures and checking for potential breaches.

“Although passwords were not leaked, scammers could piece together personal details from the exposed data to impersonate loan advisers or lure victims with promises of compensation for the data breaches,” an official at the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) said.

body.head: What to watch next
body.text: The lesson for anyone running agents in KYC, coding or credit decisions is that the efficiency case and the exposure case are now the same case: whatever an agent can read or move, something else is trying to read or move too. So before the next productivity number comes in, check whether the same systems have been tested against exactly that.

suggestion: A line on how your own shop is weighing the DNB-style efficiency case against the Korea-style exposure case would land well at the end here.
